title: The Silent Hollow
premise: Sable Ravensworth has survived fifteen years in the magic-outlawed city of Corvane by stealing memories and selling them as harmless charms, keeping his own gift hidden. When a mute child arrives at his door speaking the Hollowtongue—a language that predates kingdoms and carries living memory in every word—Sable realizes the girl is a vessel of the old magic the city's Wardens were built to destroy. Hunted by Warden-Captain Ilse Varrow, who secretly hungers for that power herself, Sable must choose between erasing the child's memories to save them both or carrying the secret to the mountain sanctuary where it could reignite the ancient war between memory-keepers and memory-eaters. In the end, Sable sacrifices his own stolen hoard of memories to seal the Hollowtongue within himself, becoming the last living archive, while the child goes free and the long winter breaks over a city that will never know what it was spared.
about_author: Sebastian Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who survive by keeping secrets, and lives somewhere he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On the eve of the winter markets, Sable sells a memory-charm to a grieving widow and reflects on the rules that keep him invisible: never steal from Wardens, never sell a whole life, never be remembered. The emotional beat is weary discipline—the quiet cost of fifteen years of small betrayals.

chapters.title: A Knock Before the Frost
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A six-year-old girl appears at his door during the first snow, mute except for words in a language Sable shouldn't understand but does—Hollowtongue, the speech of the old memory-keepers. When she touches his hand, he glimpses her fragmented past: a burned village, a fleeing mother. The beat is dread wrapped in reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Warden-Captain Ilse Varrow, investigating the village fire upriver. Ilse finds a survivor's account of 'a child who remembers too loud' and recognizes the signature of Hollowtongue—magic her order exists to erase, and power she privately craves. The beat is cold ambition sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable tries to teach the girl, whom he names Wren, to hide her gift, but her presence unravels his charms—customers begin remembering things they paid to forget. His fence, Odell, warns him someone is asking questions. The beat is the illusion of control cracking; survival now has a price he can't pay alone.

chapters.title: Memories He Should Not Own
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback-heavy. Forced to open his hidden hoard of stolen memories to find clues about Hollowtongue, Sable confronts fragments of his own past—including the memory he stole from himself the night his family died. The beat is grief excavated: he learns he once swore an oath to the keepers he abandoned.

chapters.title: The Warden's Net
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Using Odell as bait, Ilse traces the charm trade back to Sable's door. She doesn't arrest him—she offers a bargain: deliver the child, and his crimes are forgotten. Sable refuses, and Ilse lets him go, knowing fear will do her work. The beat is the trap closing softly, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Flight Across the White Fields
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sable flees with Wren toward the mountain sanctuary of Hollowmere, pursued by Wardens through blizzard country. Wren finally speaks plainly, revealing she chose Sable deliberately—he is the last keeper's oath-son. The beat is trust forged under pursuit, and the first hint that Wren understands more than any child should.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Empty Halls
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They reach the sanctuary and find it slaughtered years ago—one keeper left alive, dying, who tells Sable the truth: the war never ended; the Wardens are its inheritors, and Wren is the living archive of everything they destroyed. The beat is despair transmuted into resolve; there is no one left to save them but Sable.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Ilse corners them at the sanctuary gates as the deepest cold of winter falls. She offers Wren power-sharing, then force; Sable fights not with magic but with memory itself, flooding Ilse with the stolen lives in his hoard until she drowns in what she wanted. The beat is terrible justice outside any law—and its cost: the hoard is spent.

chapters.title: The Last Archive
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue-near. To keep Hollowtongue from dying or spreading, Sable takes Wren's burden into himself, becoming the final living archive, his own past dissolving in exchange. He wakes in spring with no family, no crimes, no oath—only a child's hand in his and a word in a dead language he somehow still knows. The beat is bittersweet renewal: the price of survival, finally paid in full.
